history_policy: Published artifacts retain their original schema and bytes. Any incompatible identity, normalization, metric, stability, or claim-boundary change creates a new profile version.
claim_boundary: Only normalized retired instructions and exact allocation replay are scored across frozen input widths. Wall time, CPU time, RSS, cycles, energy, and thermal observations are retained from the embedded exact-parent artifacts as diagnostics and cannot support a throughput, latency, energy, or full-efficiency claim.
publication_guards: every input is a complete validated exact-parent artifact with identical parent, candidate, dependency, binary, source, toolchain, host, sample-count, mode, and lane identities
the candidate first parent exactly equals the named parent in every input
at least three strictly increasing widths map exactly to the declared workload family prefix
parent and candidate execute the same positive logical-job count and checksum at each width
every retired-instruction observation is measured, positive, normalized by logical jobs, and at or below five-percent relative standard deviation per variant and width
allocation requests and allocated bytes are measured, non-negative safe integers, and exact across repeated samples within each variant and width

all original exact-parent samples, metric states, quality fields, power states, thermal states, commands boundaries, and rejected full-efficiency summaries remain embedded without sample removal or substitution
rendered adjacent and first-to-last growth ratios are derived from normalized instruction medians and make no wall-time, throughput, latency, cycle, energy, or thermal claim
